subject: Post-discovery: Ledgerly model-eval plan, golden set & temporary version freeze
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@ledgerly.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-06-15T16:10:00Z
Subject: Post-discovery: Ledgerly model-eval plan, golden set & temporary version freeze

Hi Sanjay / Priya —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a shared plan: 

- Goal: Validate model fit for Ledgerly transaction categorization (priority: precision on Merchant/Category mapping, recall for edge cases, and consistent handling of ambiguous descriptions).
- Short-term risk: you called out occasional label flips after the vendor model update last month — want to protect from regressions during our trial.

Proposed immediate actions (so we can move to a short eval without surprises):
1) You’ll share a representative prompt set and a small golden regression set (10–20 examples with desired labels) — thanks for confirming you can send that.
2) Redwood will run a focused eval on two candidate serving variants and one conservative baseline (details below) and return: per-class precision/recall, confusion slices, and the top 10 behavioral diffs relative to your golden set.
3) Temporary version freeze: we’ll snapshot the current production variant we use for the trial and request a short-term ‘version freeze’ in your environment while the eval runs and initial results are reviewed. This is to avoid unexpected vendor-side updates during test windows.
4) If diffs exceed the agreed thresholds (we’ll propose thresholds in the eval packet), we’ll recommend either pinning the snapshot for your trial or a staged rollback.

Candidate variants Redwood will evaluate (recommended):
- rw-infer-13B-quant (balanced throughput, conservative decoding)
- rw-instruct-7B-v2 (smaller, good few-shot consistency)
- baseline: your current vendor-serving snapshot (we’ll compare behaviourally)

Attachments: ledgerly_sample_prompts.json (sample prompts you can confirm), golden_regression_set.csv (placeholder until you send your version).

Next steps: Sanjay — send the CSV/labels and a list of 50 representative prompts by end of today if possible. Marissa/Aditya — once we have the data I suggest a 48-hour fast-pass evaluation and a short scoreboard for the customer.

Thanks — Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@ledgerly.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@ledgerly.com>
Date: 2028-06-15T18:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-discovery: Ledgerly model-eval plan, golden set & temporary version freeze

Vivek —

Appreciate the clear plan. Quick notes:
- Attached is our initial prompt set (ledgerly_prompts_v1.json) and a starter golden_regression_set.csv with 25 rows (we flagged 8 high-risk examples where prior model flips happened).
- We are comfortable with a temporary version freeze for the trial window; I’ll coordinate with infra to hold updates for 72 hours from the evaluation start.
- For thresholds: can you propose concrete numbers? We typically want precision >= 0.92 for core categories and no more than 6% delta in high-risk examples.

Also attaching a scrap of logs where the vendor update changed category for ‘PAYPAL *NETFLIX’ from ‘Subscription’ to ‘Misc’ — that’s the sort of regression we want to detect automatically.

Sanjay
Sanjay Rao
Head of Product, Ledgerly
Attachments: ledgerly_prompts_v1.json, golden_regression_set.csv, vendor_log_snippet.txt

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@ledgerly.com>
Date: 2028-06-15T20:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-discovery: Ledgerly model-eval plan, golden set & temporary version freeze

Quick operational plan from Redwood side:

1) Eval scope & targets
- Run the three variants Vivek listed against Ledgerly’s prompt set + your golden_regression_set (25 rows).
- Metrics: per-class precision/recall, F1, and a simple behavioral-diff score (we compute token-level and label-change diffs).

2) Concrete thresholds (proposal) — please review and confirm with Ledgerly:
- Core categories: precision >= 0.92 and recall >= 0.88
- High-risk examples (those 8 flagged): no more than 4 misclassifications out of 8 (<=50% would be terrible; we want stricter tolerance) — propose max 2 misclassifications allowed.
- Overall label-shift: delta <= 3% compared to your current baseline snapshot.

3) Snapshot & temporary freeze
- Aditya will trigger a production snapshot of the variant we route to Ledgerly’s trial and create a model artifact tag (ldg-2028-snapshot-1). We’ll request Ledgerly hold vendor-side updates for the 72-hour window starting when evaluation begins.

4) Deliverables (timeline)
- T+0 (we have assets): Redwood runs fast-pass eval (24–48h).
- T+48: deliver evaluation packet (CSV with per-example verdicts, diff highlights, top 10 behavioral regressions) + recommendation (pin snapshot OR reconfigure decoding/temperature).
- T+72: if pin recommended, create a plan for staged rollout with rollback steps and cost/latency tradeoffs.

5) Ask for Ledgerly: add the 50 representative prompts and confirm the 72-hour freeze window. Also confirm if there are any categories you’d like prioritized for manual review.

I’ll draft the eval job and schedule compute tonight so we can start as soon as they confirm.

—Marissa
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: eval_benchmarks_summary.pdf (template), proposed_thresholds.md

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@ledgerly.com>
Date: 2028-06-16T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-discovery: Ledgerly model-eval plan, golden set & temporary version freeze

Confirming operational steps I executed this morning: 
- Created production snapshot: model artifact tag = ldg-2028-snapshot-1 (saved weights, tokenizer, decode config).
- Launched eval job on rw-infer-13B-quant and rw-instruct-7B-v2; baseline will be the vendor snapshot provided in the CSV.
- Uploaded Ledgerly prompt set and golden CSV to shared Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/Shared/LDG-2028/EvalPack (permissions set to view for sanjay@ledgerly.com).
- Kicked off automated behavioral-diff job; it will produce: token-diff matrix, per-example label diff, and a ranked list of the top 10 behavioral regressions.

If metrics exceed thresholds, I’ll prepare a short decision memo recommending either: pin the snapshot for the trial (ldg-2028-snapshot-1) or a conservative configuration change (temperature/decoding tweaks) to bring classification stability in line.

Estimated ETA for fast-pass packet: 36 hours from job start (so by 2028-06-17T21:00:00Z). I’ll post the raw CSVs and the summary PDF to the Drive.

If Ledgerly wants a stricter safety net during the trial, we can also enable a live-guard that routes edge-case confidence scores to a manual review queue. Let me know and I’ll include cost/latency impact in the memo.

Aditya Rao
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: ldg-2028-snapshot-1.meta (artifact stub)
